biography.summary: Donya Caoimhe Yazdani is a fictional NeverBeen digital model and imagined creative professional in an alternate universe. In this version of her story, the city she calls home is Mashhad, Iran; the neighbourhood and every biographical detail below are invented for this fictional character. After earning a fictional Bachelor of Design in Spatial Practice, she spent her early career in architecture and spatial design with Open Courtyard Workshop and later Civic Form Studio, building experience in spatial composition, model-making, human-centred design. Today she works as an independent model and creative collaborator in the NeverBeen Multiverse, bringing her creative training into editorial, fashion and travel-led stories. Donya's passions in this fictional timeline include accessible arts education and low-waste production, among other personal causes, and she enjoys dance classes, museum afternoons, analogue journaling in her time away from sets and studios. Her ambitions in this imagined storyline are to build a thoughtful creative label for emerging artists, to help make fashion and image-making more responsible without losing a sense of play, and to leave every collaboration more generous than she found it. The relationship status recorded for her in this chapter is "single"; the people, places and milestones below are entirely invented and exist only in the NeverBeen Multiverse.
earlyLife: In this alternate-universe story, Donya Caoimhe Yazdani was born on 13 April 2001 at 17:32 Asia/Tehran at the fictional NeverBeen House of Birth in Kūh-e Sangi, Mashhad, Iran. The venue, date, time and every childhood episode are invented; no real address or medical record is represented.

At age four, around 2005, a slow family breakfast and the familiar rooms of home became the first small landmarks in her imagined life. The accompanying mobile-camera scene is a fictional memory, not an archival photograph.

By age eight, around 2009, she had begun exploring the nearby streets with her fictional mother Simin Yazdani, noticing rain-dark pavement, shop shutters and changing light. That curiosity gradually became a habit of observation.

In secondary school, around age sixteen in 2017, she found confidence in friends and hands-on class projects. These school scenes are fictional snapshots from the character’s timeline, not records of a real school or child.
